title: Waterslides, flumes and receiving pools
audience: Pool and waterslide operators, attendants and technicians at public waterslide facilities in SA. Electrical work on lighting or wiring is licensed where a licence applies. Figures apply under the state standard.
learningOutcomes: Describe the minimum staffing and sight-line requirements for a waterslide.
State the daily flume inspection and the closure rule for a faulty flume.
Describe the receiving pool and turnover requirements, and the bather warnings that must be displayed.

instruction.heading: Staffing and sight lines
instruction.body: The standard sets minimum attendant positions for a waterslide. One observer must stand at the head of each flume to supervise riders entering it. A second observer must stand at the receiving pool to supervise riders leaving the flume and emerging from the water. Each observer needs a clear line of sight along the whole run, or a signal device telling the top attendant that the next rider can go. A communication system has to connect the attendants at each end.

instruction.heading: Daily inspection and closure
instruction.body: Each day, before use, the entire flume needs inspecting for faults or damage that could injure users. If the inspection finds a faulty or damaged flume, the slide shuts until repairs are complete. The fee arrangement should not reward riders for running or horseplay in order to fit in extra rides.

instruction.heading: Design checks an operator should look for
instruction.body: Starting points need sturdy handrails, a grip-friendly floor and either a canopy of about two metres or another device that regulates entry. The flume must keep riders within the slide at any speed, and designers should steer clear of sharp turns and rapid runs of drops and curves. The flume's end must discharge into a receiving pool with water depth of between 900 mm and 1 m, and that depth has to reach at least three metres out ahead of the flume. Pool surrounds should measure no less than 1.2 m across, light-coloured, impervious and non-slip, and the pool colour must let staff see every rider.

instruction.heading: Turnover, flow and make-up water
instruction.body: A waterslide pool needs its entire volume filtered no less often than hourly, given the heavy bather load. Roughly four-fifths of the flow should come off through the overflow channels and skimmers, and about one-fifth from below the surface. A self-filling make-up system has to hold the working level. Where turnover requirements vary, a separate filter is recommended.

instruction.heading: Warnings that must be displayed
instruction.body: A sign must sit prominently at the entry and at the flume. It tells riders to leave the pool immediately on discharge, limits tandem riding to adults with small children, forbids horseplay and carrying glass or pointed items, and asks riders to remove jewellery and glasses that could cause injury. It advises that people who are pregnant, who have weak limbs or a weak back, who have heart ailments, or who have any condition that could be worsened by use, should not use the slide. It also lets management turn people away.

procedure: Confirm the observers are in place at the head of each flume and at the receiving pool, and that the communication system works.
Inspect the whole flume before opening, and record the result.
Check the receiving pool depth, the make-up water level and the turnover record.
Confirm the warning signs are displayed at the entry and at the flume.
Close the flume immediately if the inspection finds a fault, and report it to the operator.

workedExamples.situation: During the morning inspection of a waterslide, a flume joint is found to have a sharp edge at one connection. The first rider is queuing at the top.
workedExamples.reasoning: The standard requires a faulty or damaged flume to be closed until it is repaired. Stop the first rider, close the flume, put the closure in writing, and report the joint to the operator for repair before reopening.

equipmentAndPpe: Inspection checklist for the full flume length
Communication radios or intercom for attendants
Spare warning signs in good condition
Non-slip footwear and eye protection around water

commonErrors.error: Sending a rider before the top observer signals the slide is clear.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the clear-flume signal or device before every rider.

commonErrors.error: Skipping the daily flume inspection on a busy day.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect the full flume before use, every day.

commonErrors.error: Letting one observer cover both the top and the receiving pool.
commonErrors.prevention: Staff both positions and keep the communication system working.

commonErrors.error: Allowing rough riding to increase throughput.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not run fees or queues that reward rough or boisterous riding.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A faulty or damaged flume must be closed until repaired. Injury risk is serious, so the closure is not optional.
Riders who are pregnant, have weak limbs or a weak back, have heart ailments or have related conditions should not use the slide. Keep the warning sign visible and enforce it.
Electrical wiring and lighting have to meet the wiring standard the state standard names, and electrical work is licensed where a licence applies. This lesson does not grant a licence.
Figures are South Australian standard values (revised 2013). Confirm the current regulation text.

qualityStandard: Observers are in place at both ends of each flume, with a working communication system.
The full flume is inspected each day before use, and any fault closes the slide.
Warning signs are present and legible, and turnover is recorded against the one-hour limit.
documentationEvidence: Daily flume inspection record with date, time, result and inspector
Attendant roster and communication check record
summary: Two observers per flume and a working communication system.
Inspect the full flume every day, and close it for any fault.
Receiving pool depth of 900 mm to 1 m, turnover at least every hour, and warning signs at the entry and the flume.

knowledgeChecks.question: How often must a waterslide pool's whole volume be filtered, under the standard?
A flume is found to have a damaged section during the morning inspection. What does the standard require?
options: Close the waterslide until it is repaired
Operate at half speed with the sign up
Put up a sign and open anyway for the morning

knowledgeChecks.question: How many observers does the standard set as the minimum for a waterslide with one flume?
options: None, because the slide is self-supervising and no staff are rostered
One, at the receiving pool only and one for the sign-in desk
Two, one at the head of the flume and one at the receiving pool
Four, one for each corner of the pool and a lifeguard on the tower
